What is a Roth IRA?

A Roth IRA is a US retirement account you pay into with money you already paid tax on, so qualified withdrawals in retirement are tax-free.

Updated Nov 2, 2026

Who can open a Roth IRA?

Anyone with earned income under the yearly limit can open one at most brokers. You choose the investments inside it, such as index funds or ETFs, and they grow without yearly tax on gains.

How much can you put in each year?

There is a yearly contribution limit set by the IRS, and it changes over time. Check the current limit before you contribute, and remember the limit is shared across all your IRAs.

When can you take money out?

You can take out what you put in at any time. Earnings are tax-free after age 59 and a half once the account is five years old. Taking earnings out early can mean tax and a penalty.
